clue.text: A day off? Yes and no!

definitions.text: A day off? Yes and no!

parts.words: A day off? Yes and no!
parts.note: a day taken off work while claiming illness: it is time off, yet officially it is not meant to be a holiday

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether some absence really counts as leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word for a day off falsely claimed as sick leave, so it is and is not a genuine day off.

clue.text: Community also developed outside Channel Islands

definitions.note: used adjectivally, as in community centre

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the islands' abbreviation
developed suggests the letters being worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A community too has grown up around the Channel Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Community' is read adjectivally, as in community centre or social centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to society, as in a social club or community club; adjective synonym.

clue.text: Temporary manager's oddly keen in frantic rat race

indicators.note: those odd letters go inside the rearranged letters
frantic signals the letters being thrown into wild disorder
picks the odd-numbered letters of keen

explanation.surface: An interim boss is strangely eager in the hectic corporate rat race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantic' rearranges RATRACE; 'oddly' gives KE from keen.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, an interim boss is called this; an idiom for someone holding the post until a permanent appointment.

clue.text: Cool African party breaking into safe with poorer person providing cover

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the poorer word is added on after the rest

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool

indicators.note: the party goes inside the safe word

parts.note: sure means safe, certain
the ANC is the African National Congress
broker, more broke, means poorer

explanation.surface: A burglary: a gang breaks into a safe with an accomplice keeping lookout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'safe' suggests a strongbox but means sure; 'cover' means insurance.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent who arranges policies gives people cover against loss; a cryptic description of the profession.

clue.text: Model European member of parliament left in gallery

indicators.note: the European, politician and left letters sit inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A European politician's model is left on show in an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of major British art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern or guide to copy from is a model; synonym as nouns.

clue.text: Ring back?

parts.note: a sound that rings back is one that reverberates or is repeated off a surface

explanation.definitionFit: A reverberation is sound sent back, ringing out again; cryptic description posing as a phone request.

clue.text: Tipsy UK penpal pinches food found in tins

indicators.note: tipsy means drunk, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: pinches here is fodder, its letters joining the pool

explanation.surface: A drunk British correspondent steals snacks from the cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinches' looks like the container indicator but its letters are part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinned tropical fruit pieces are a typical canned food; description of an example.

clue.text: A politician once needing independent defence in law

parts.note: Lib, a Liberal, was an old British party member, now Lib Dem

explanation.surface: A former politician needs an independent defence in court.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Party merged into the Liberal Democrats in 1988, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea of having been elsewhere when a crime was committed is a legal defence.

clue.text: Ingredient of meringue, for example, with weight adjusted

indicators.note: with means accompanied by, so the rearranged weight letters follow the example abbreviation
adjusted shows the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe note about adjusting the weight of meringue ingredients.
explanation.definitionFit: Meringue is made of whisked albumen and sugar; example of an ingredient.

clue.text: Bob is short, and scarcely lacking heart

parts.note: curt means short or brusque in manner

indicators.note: the word scarcely loses all its middle letters, keeping only its outside pair

explanation.surface: A description of someone's haircut being cropped and barely there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a haircut or a name, but it means a quick bow or dip.
explanation.definitionFit: To bob is to make a quick bending movement, like the respectful dip of the knees made to royalty.

clue.text: Judgment of relations enveloped in obsession

indicators.note: the relations word is wrapped inside the obsession word

parts.note: to have a thing about something is to be obsessed with it
kin are one's relations or family

explanation.surface: Someone's opinion on their relatives clouded by fixation.
explanation.definitionFit: One's current thinking is one's opinion or judgment on a matter; synonym in the sense of view.

clue.text: Smile in confusion about sport and poor governance

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed around the sport
the letters of smile are muddled

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A confused smile about sport and bad government.
explanation.walkthrough: RU, rugby union, is a standard crossword shorthand for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad or unjust rule of a country is poor government; synonym.

clue.text: A new editor's rock

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of the following word are made anew in another order

explanation.surface: A newly appointed newspaper editor's dependable stone.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'editor's' is ignored: its S belongs to the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor planet is a lump of rock orbiting the Sun; the answer is an example of a space rock.

clue.text: Disappear — like a commercial vehicle?

parts.note: a van is a commercial vehicle for goods
the suffix -ish means like or somewhat

explanation.surface: Asking whether vanishing resembles a delivery van.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish is to go out of sight suddenly; plain synonym.

clue.text: In the best case, island truly needs to replace leader with daughter

indicators.note: the first letter is swapped out for the following letter

parts.note: really means truly

explanation.surface: An island truly needs a daughter, not a leader, to take charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverb meaning in a perfect world or under the best circumstances; synonym.

clue.text: Like-minded individual, loving wine and whisky, say

parts.note: kind means affectionate or loving
red is short for red wine
whisky is an example of a spirit, hence 'say'

explanation.surface: A soulmate who loves wine and whisky too.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shares your outlook and tastes is a soulmate, a person of like mind.

clue.text: Provided support, but surly about cutting grass

indicators.note: the surly and about letters cut into the grass word

parts.note: reed is a tall grass
sour means surly
C, circa, means about

explanation.surface: Help is given, but grudgingly, while mowing grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To be resourced is to be supplied with funds or materials, given backing; synonym.

clue.text: Reclaim it at establishment admitting copies

indicators.note: the phrase admits, or holds within it, the letters needed

explanation.surface: An instruction to recover something at a firm which admits fakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy someone is to mimic them; synonym verb.

clue.text: Promote boss's best products?

parts.note: to market a product is to promote it
a leader is a boss; with the possessive 's it gives the plural letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to advertise the manager's finest goods.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'boss's' is read as part of the word, giving LEADERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Brands that sell most in their sector lead the market, so the top-selling goods fit the description.

clue.text: Safest going out for meals?

indicators.note: going out suggests the letters dispersed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Is eating out the safest option for meals?
explanation.definitionFit: Banquets, large elaborate meals; synonym.

clue.text: Bolt wears little sleeveless tunic

indicators.note: the little word puts the bolt word on, so the bolt word goes inside it

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
a bar is a bolt across a door

explanation.surface: Usain Bolt the sprinter dressed in a small vest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' suggests the Jamaican sprinter, but it is the door fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald's or medieval knight's short open-sided coat over armour; the term names this garment exactly.

clue.text: Green stuff produced in tidal inlets, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that it is the sound of the word that counts

parts.note: bays are inlets of the sea

explanation.surface: Green seaweed growing in coastal inlets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green stuff' suggests seaweed or money; it is the cloth on snooker tables.
explanation.definitionFit: Woollen cloth usually dyed green, used on billiard and card tables; a green fabric.

clue.text: Local area parasite must drink meths regularly

indicators.note: the parasite takes the other letters into itself, as if swallowing them

parts.note: a louse is a parasitic insect

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of meths

explanation.surface: A grim scene of a down-and-out drinking methylated spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of METHS are E and H, placed in LOUSE after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: A British local is one's nearby pub, and a pub is an old-style beer-selling inn.

clue.text: Floor enthusiasts given a lift

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting means reading the letters upwards

parts.note: nuts are enthusiasts, as in sports nuts

explanation.surface: Fans lifted up off the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floor' looks like a noun but is a verb: to knock down.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to knock them out or astound them; verb synonym.

clue.text: Set off alongside dense woods

indicators.note: the set letters are placed alongside the dense word

parts.note: thick means dense

indicators.note: off suggests the letters going wrong, rearranged

explanation.surface: Setting out through dense woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: Small dense woods or copses of trees and shrubs; near-synonym.

clue.text: Represents good person joining staff in recession

indicators.note: going backwards, so the combined letters are read from end to start
the two pieces are joined into one string

parts.note: ST, saint, is crossword shorthand for a good person
a cane is a walking staff

explanation.surface: An economic tale of a worthy person joining a workforce during a downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' suggests employees; it is a stick. STCANE read backwards is ENACTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact a role is to act it out or portray it; synonym.

clue.text: Cutting last of remarks before trial

indicators.note: the letter is placed ahead of the trial word
takes only the final letter of remarks

parts.note: a hearing is a trial in court

explanation.surface: A lawyer's final comment ahead of a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipping, as of sheep's fleece; synonym as a verb form.

clue.text: Comments from assistants besieging head of security

indicators.note: the assistants surround the letter as an army surrounds a town

parts.note: aides are assistants

indicators.note: the first letter of security

explanation.surface: Remarks from staff surrounding the chief of security.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks made in an undertone or a digression; synonym.
